focus: Snapshot requires the Application UI owner, which can drain on another native event thread. It uses the allocation/viewport of the last completed canvas Render; it does not flush a pending native resize. Render calls size()/syncCamera() under Application.Do and the originating native window mutex, after its own layout. Snapshot holds that same application owner and native mutex, and calls Sync, which validates Model and calls updateCamera()->syncCamera() using current Model.View. No raw widget Geom/ContentBBox read occurs in Snapshot. The platform smoke waits for Render to publish a requested size, validates image dimensions against Model.View, and makes immediate zoom/center edits and pixel assertions inside the same owner callback before another Render can enter.

WindowByName registry iteration uses AppMulti.Mu, but Window.Name/SetName are plain field access. newRenderWindow sets the name after system.NewWindow publishes the registry. This finding was fixed rather than refuted: the platform CLI contains no WindowByName calls. It waits for second-window Snapshot frame readiness and captures the first native handle on the application owner before closing it. Desktop Window.IsClosed reads composerPointer.Load atomically; native teardown withdraws that composer before releasing resources.

The original prepared core/renderwindow.go already imports system/composer. The added redraw tests use the owned TestWindow test fixture from patch17. Patch19 is separate and does not rewrite patches17/18. Its CanRedraw admission retains images.used through End and resets at Start, refusing borrowed native texture replay while allowing later raster-only batches. The focused GPU/composer/core regression log records go test -race -count=1 and successful exit.

The CLI complete field denotes full OS qualification rather than basic smoke success. Runtime smoke exits0 after all recorded basic checks, while qualification gaps and complete=false remain because target-specific adapters and external/hardware acceptance are unqualified. --require-complete fails with exit2 on those gaps. Native logs identify macOS only; host API fixtures and pure helper crosscompile are not actual Windows/Linux driver execution.

ValidateFileOptions starts by calling app.FileOptions.Validate and returning any error before its alphanumeric punctuation loop. app/services.go:41 rejects ext==empty and any dot/space/slash/backslash for every extension. Both Windows nativeChooseFile and LinuxFileArgs call ValidateFileOptions before helper execution, so empty extensions never reach a chooser. The separate narrow loop then excludes non-ASCII glob punctuation. The claimed empty-string acceptance overlooks that initial shared validation call.

Application.CloseWindow cancels the registered window context synchronously under a.mu before removing it. When the last registered window closes, it calls closeLocked under that same mutex, which synchronously calls a.cancel() before returning. Thus the final secondLife.Err()/a.Context().Err() assertion checks logical lifetime cancellation, which is complete before CloseWindow returns; native teardown remains asynchronous and is awaited by Driver.Run/core.Wait. The smoke distinguishes these operations and does not claim that those Err reads prove physical teardown.
